messages.text:
"Create an ultra-detailed, hyper-immersive, expansive, long-form, and production-ready 3D detailed pixel-art horror and open-world wilderness exploration game titled \"Ape Project\". The entire game world spans a massive 500x500 meter open-world jungle map featuring slightly rolling, hilly terrain, dense canopy foliage, natural valleys, and sparse tactical cover points. The game features absolutely zero missions, zero rigid objectives, and zero structured goals; the core experience focuses entirely on pure, open-ended roaming, continuous atmospheric exploration, and stealth survival. The game must be rendered strictly through high-end 3D low-poly engines textured with crisp, high-definition 3D pixel-art assets, dynamic retro lighting shaders, atmospheric volumetric fog rolling over the terrain, and precise voxel grid layouts, completely avoiding flat 2D sprites or modern high-poly realism.
1. Massive Open-World Jungle Map Architecture (500x500M)
Wilderness Scale @COMMENT_BODY@ Scope: A sprawling 500x500 meter dense outdoor jungle environment designed with natural elevation changes, hilly topography, winding valleys, and scattered 3D pixel-art trees built purely for endless roaming and atmospheric wilderness survival.
Environmental Design: Hand-crafted 3D pixel textures for organic tree trunks, mossy ground terrain, damp foliage, rolling volumetric fog, and dynamic shadow casting across the forest floor.
2. Player Character Model @COMMENT_BODY@ Animation (Lethal Ape Style)
Player Model: A detailed 3D pixel-art ape character model directly inspired by the iconic movement mechanics and silhouette of Lethal Ape.
Locomotion Framework: Ultra-smooth pixel animation cycles for quadrupedal sprinting, upright walking, fluid climbing over hilly jungle terrain, crouching behind foliage, and responsive camera movement.
3. Dual-Apex Predator Ecosystem @COMMENT_BODY@ Tragic Lore
Entity 01: Mossman (MOSS-01)
Combat @COMMENT_BODY@ Physical Stats:
Height: 2.8 meters.  
Speed: 33 km/h.  
Turning Agility: 50% • Wide Arcs.  
Vision: None - Blind.  
Hearing: Super Sensitive.  
Abilities: Echo Hunt, Spore Trail, Blind Charge.  
Tragic Backstory: Mossman was a research monkey sent into the canopy floor to sample soil. One afternoon it walked too close to a seep of compound MOSSER, slipped, and fell in. The spill rewrote it: dense chlorophyll skin, thirty percent mass gain, and optic nerves that reabsorbed into a wider auditory cortex. It cannot see you. It hears a footstep across sixty metres of wet jungle, and it holds 33 km/h on the way there.  
Entity 02: Warden
Combat @COMMENT_BODY@ Physical Stats:
Height: 1.9 meters.  
Speed: 30.8 km/h.  
Turning Agility: 75% • Poor.  
Vision: None - Blind.  
Hearing: Extreme Range.  
Abilities: Mosser Mask, Xenon Hands, Long Ear.  
Tragic Backstory: Warden used to be a forest ranger. One patrol it walked out to check a Mosser seep where the Xenon drums had split, lost its footing on the moss and went in face first. The liquid took its eyes and kept going. The face that crawls out of the water now is one wet green mask with a mouth in it, and the hands are caked in Mosser and Xenon with crystals pushing out of the knuckles. It cannot see you. It hears a snapped twig from two hundred metres and does not stop until the sound stops.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.
